info.name: Morning Brief v2 — Voice API
info.description:
Chatterbox-Turbo voice service.

**Before you start:** run `GET /voices` once — it lists the reference clips and auto-selects the `voice` variable for the other requests.

**Addresses**
- Same machine: `http://127.0.0.1:8090`
- LAN: `http://10.0.0.130:8090`

**Pauses & tags** — write these straight into `text`:
- `[[pause:0.8]]` silence for that many seconds (max 5)
- `...` or a blank line — one beat (default 0.45s)
- `[sigh]`, `[chuckle]`, `[laugh]`, `[cough]`, `[gasp]`, `[groan]`, `[sniffle]`, `[yawn]`

**Audio requests:** use **Send and Download** in Postman to save the `.wav`.

variable.description: The voice service. Use http://127.0.0.1:8090 when Postman runs on the Mac itself.
Reference clip name, without the .wav extension. GET /voices sets this automatically.

exec: pm.test('device is mps or cpu', () => pm.expect(['mps', 'cpu']).to.include(d.device));
console.log('device:', d.device, '| default voice:', d.default_voice, '| clips:', d.clips);

request.description: Model, device and reference status. The first call after a restart takes ~40s while the model warms up.

exec: pm.test('at least one usable clip', () => pm.expect(usable.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Reference clips on disk. A clip must be longer than 5 seconds to be usable. This request sets the `voice` collection variable to the first usable clip.

item.name: Synthesize — WAV with pauses and a tag

request.description:
Returns audio/wav. Use **Send and Download** to save the file.

Response headers: `X-Duration`, `X-Voice`, `X-Sample-Rate`.

item.name: Synthesize — short pause and tag test

request.description: The quickest check that pauses and tags work — about 4 seconds of audio. `beat` overrides the default ellipsis/paragraph pause of 0.45s.
Builds the built-in sample bulletin. Returns JSON: `duration`, `spans`, `marks` (start/end per beat), `warnings`, and the audio as base64. The Test tab prints the timing table to the Postman console.
